logline: 정직한 나무꾼과 욕심쟁이 이웃이 같은 연못에서 다른 대답을 한다
destination: 전래동화 금도끼 은도끼에서 만날 수 있습니다
setting: 조선의 산 중턱과 폭포 아래 연못
anchor: a Korean boy of about ten in hemp clothes, his small sister beside him
palette: deep pine green, misty white, warm gold, iron grey, hanji cream

woodcutter.desc: a lean Joseon woodcutter in his thirties, face browned by mountain sun with high cheekbones and steady dark eyes, a faded indigo cotton band tied around his head to keep the sweat back; he wears a patched jeogori jacket of undyed hemp open at the throat, hemp trousers bound at the calf with cloth leggings, and straw sandals worn thin at the heel; his hands are broad and rope-calloused, a healed scar across one thumb; his only tool is an old iron axe, the blade nicked and sharpened thin, the dark wooden haft polished by years of his grip and lately gone loose at the head; a wooden A-frame carrier stacked with split pine stands wherever he works; he moves with the economy of long labor, plants his feet wide before every swing, bows deeply from the waist when he gives thanks, and waves both open hands before his chest when he refuses a thing

spirit.desc: the old spirit of the mountain pool: a tall grandfather figure rising from the water itself, long white beard reaching his chest and long white eyebrows that shade deep calm eyes, white hair drawn up in a bare topknot open to the sky, his brow and crown unadorned; he wears layered robes of white ramie that stay dry above the waterline, wide sleeves hanging heavy and still, a sash of pale grey at the waist; below the waist his form thins into the dark green water and coiling white mist, so he stands in the pool as a candle stands in its holder; his voice is slow and level, he raises whatever he holds in one unhurried arc to the height of his beard, and his face keeps one unchanged mildness whether he offers gold or iron — only the long white brows move, and when they slide low his eyes go dark as the deep water

neighbor.desc: a stocky farmer from the same valley, round-faced with quick glittering eyes that move faster than his feet, soft unworked hands, and a small mouth pursed around constant reckoning; he wears a stiff new horsehair hat tied with a glossy ribbon, a vest of dark silk over a clean jeogori too fine for wood-cutting, and leather shoes better suited to a market street than a mountain slope; on his shoulder rides a brand-new axe, its blade mirror-bright and its pale haft still smelling of the joiner's shop; he walks leaning forward as if pulled by his own reaching hands, licks his thumb before he touches anything of value, and stands closest to whatever shines

pond.desc: a deep mountain pool at the foot of a low waterfall, its center black-green and unreadable, its rim ringed with wet mossed boulders and leaning red-barked pines; the waterfall comes down in one thin white thread that stirs the surface only at the far edge, so most of the pool lies mirror-still; cold white mist gathers over the middle water at every hour, thickening when the pool means to speak; ferns and pine roots grip the bank, pine needles float in slow spirals at the margins, and everything that enters the center water goes down out of sight at once

hillside.desc: a pine hillside above the pool in early summer: red-barked pines standing well apart on a slope of dry needles and grey outcrop stone, morning light falling in long clean bars between the trunks; fresh pale stumps and split logs mark the woodcutter's patch, wood chips bright on the brown ground, resin scenting the air; below through the trees the pool glints dark, and far down the valley small terraced fields and a thread of village smoke show the world the mountain stands over

beats.beat: 가난한 나무꾼이 산속에서 낡은 쇠도끼로 나무를 벤다
beats.visual: early summer morning on the pine hillside: long bars of light between red-barked trunks, dry needles and grey outcrop underfoot, wood chips bright around a fresh pale stump; the lean woodcutter stands mid-labor at a marked pine, feet planted wide, the old iron axe swung back over his shoulder, its nicked thin blade catching one fleck of sun and its dark haft polished by his grip; his patched hemp jeogori is open at the throat, the faded indigo band dark with sweat at his brow, calf leggings and thin straw sandals dusted with chips; beside him his wooden A-frame carrier leans loaded with split pine, rope neatly wound; below through the well-spaced trunks the dark glint of the pool shows small, and far down the valley terraced fields and one thread of village smoke lie in morning haze; resin light, clean air, a working quiet over the whole slope
beats.motion: the woodcutter swings the axe through one full unhurried stroke after another, shoulders winding and unwinding, the blade biting the same pale notch while chips flick out and tumble down the needle slope, his breath keeping the slow count of labor, the loaded carrier and the bright valley holding still behind him; with each stroke the loose head shifts a hair on the haft; the camera watches from just downslope, pushing in slowly across the chips

beats.visual: the slope's edge where the hillside drops to the mountain pool: the woodcutter has followed a leaning pine right to the bank and stands braced on a wet mossed boulder in mid-swing — but the swing has gone wrong; the loosened iron head has left the haft and hangs in the air over the water, turning, its nicked blade throwing one last fleck of light, while the bare wooden haft finishes its arc in his hands; below waits the pool, black-green and unreadable at the center, mirror-still, the thin white thread of the waterfall stirring only the far edge, cold mist lying low over the middle water; pine needles float in slow spirals at the margins, the red-barked pines lean over their own reflections, and the woodcutter's face is caught turning from effort into open dismay, eyes following the falling iron
beats.motion: the iron head sails out in one slow turning arc away from the bare haft, meets the pool's center and slides under, the black-green water closing over it while rings spread wide and wider toward the mossed rim; the woodcutter's body finishes its swing and freezes leaning after the vanished blade, the empty haft loose in his two hands, the pines hold still, and the camera follows the rings outward from the center

beats.visual: the pool's bank in flat late-morning light: the woodcutter sits sunk on a wet mossed boulder at the water's edge, shoulders fallen, the bare wooden haft lying across his two open palms like something ended; his straw sandals rest at the waterline, the faded indigo band pushed up his brow, his dark steady eyes fixed down into the black-green center where the iron went and where nothing at all shows back but his own bent reflection; behind him the A-frame carrier waits loaded on the slope, rope still neat, the day's work stopped in the middle; the waterfall's thin white thread keeps its small far sound, cold mist gathers slowly over the middle water, pine needles drift in their spirals past his feet, and the leaning red pines close the frame around one poor man, one empty haft and one unreadable pool
beats.motion: the woodcutter's shoulders sink lower by slow degrees while the empty haft turns over and over in his hands, his thumb finding the smooth worn place where the iron used to seat; his bent reflection rocks gently on the water below him, a long breath clouds faintly in the cool air over the pool, the mist beyond thickening a shade; carrier, pines and waterfall hold their places, and the camera drifts down and in toward his open palms

beats.beat: 연못이 소용돌이치며 흰 수염 신령이 떠오른다
beats.visual: the pool transformed: the middle water turns in a wide slow spiral, white mist standing up from it in coiling walls, and out of the center rises the old spirit — waist-deep in the middle of the pool, touching no bank, a tall grandfather figure lifted waist-high above the surface, long white beard to his chest, long white eyebrows shading deep calm eyes, white topknot, layered white ramie robes hanging dry and heavy above the waterline while below the waist his form thins away into dark water and mist; the surface around him mounds and sheets off in silver rings; on the bank, both feet on the mossed stone, the woodcutter has scrambled up from his boulder and stands pressed back against a pine, the empty haft clutched to his chest, mouth open, eyes wide under the indigo band; the waterfall thread glows white through the risen mist, and the whole pool holds a pale cold light of its own
beats.motion: the spirit rises in one smooth unbroken ascent, water sheeting off the mist where his robes gather, the wide spiral turning slowly around him and the silver rings running out to lap the mossed boulders; his long brows lift a degree as his calm eyes find the man on the bank; the woodcutter presses harder back against the pine bark, the haft tight to his chest, his knees giving a small tremble; the camera rises with the spirit from water level

beats.visual: the spirit stands waist-deep in the middle of the pool, risen out of the water itself with mist where his legs would be, the woodcutter stays on the bank with both feet planted on the mossed stone, dry, the pool in its pale mist-light, spirit and man facing each other across the water: the spirit's right arm is lifted to the height of his white beard, and in his hand hangs a Korean woodcutter's axe of solid gold, its short thick wooden haft no longer than a forearm and its head a broad heavy wedge, mirror-bright, throwing a warm yellow gleam that lies out over the black-green water in one long bar and touches the woodcutter's astonished face; the wide ramie sleeve has slid back from the spirit's pale wrist, his deep eyes rest level on the man, mild and unreadable under the long white brows; the woodcutter stands at the waterline on the mossed boulder, empty haft hanging in one hand now, his face lit gold from below, eyes round, lips parted between awe and honest confusion; mist coils between them, the waterfall thread burns white behind, and every pine around the pool leans in over its own gilded reflection
beats.motion: the golden axe is already raised and stays completely motionless at the height of the spirit's beard for the whole shot, its warm gleam lying steady on the water; only the man moves — the woodcutter's breath goes shallow, his free hand rising halfway toward the shine before he masters it and draws it back; mist keeps coiling between them, and the camera slides slowly along the bar of gold light from axe to face

beats.visual: the spirit stands waist-deep in the middle of the pool, risen out of the water itself with mist where his legs would be, the woodcutter stays on the bank with both feet planted on the mossed stone, dry, close on the two of them across the water, the golden axe still raised between: the woodcutter has straightened himself on the boulder and bows his head aside while both his open hands wave before his chest in the plain polite refusal of a countryman, palms out, fingers spread, the empty haft tucked under one arm; his sun-browned face is respectful and completely certain, eyes lowered from the gold, mouth shaping the honest word; opposite him the spirit watches from within the standing mist, beard and robes utterly still, the axe's gleam lying now unclaimed on the water between them like a bridge with only one willing end; the mossed boulders, the floating needles and the leaning pines hold the frame around this small exchange, and the pale mist-light makes the man's worn hemp and the god's white ramie the two poles of the picture
beats.motion: the woodcutter's head turns aside in one slow deliberate shake and back, and again, while his open hands wave crosswise before his chest in the small steady rhythm of refusal, the golden axe hangs unmoved in the spirit's grip, its gleam rippling faintly on the water between them, the mist drifting a hand's width; the spirit's long brows hold their calm line, and the camera creeps in past the raised gold toward the man's honest bent face

beats.visual: the spirit stands waist-deep in the middle of the pool, risen out of the water itself with mist where his legs would be, the woodcutter stays on the bank with both feet planted on the mossed stone, dry, seen from behind the spirit's white shoulder and wide sleeve: his arm holds out a Korean woodcutter's axe of solid silver, its short thick wooden haft no longer than a forearm and its head a broad heavy wedge over the water, its broad head mirror-bright and throwing a pale cold sheen like winter light; past the silver, across the pool, the woodcutter stands small and clear on his mossed boulder, bent forward from the waist in a deep respectful bow, both hands flat on his thighs, the empty haft leaning against his leg, the indigo band and patched hemp humble against all that shine; his face, tilted up just enough to be honest with the spirit's eyes, carries the same certainty as before; the pool lies black-green and still under the crossing bar of silver light, mist walls standing soft at either side, the waterfall thread white and thin between the leaning pines at the far rim
beats.motion: the silver axe rests completely motionless in the spirit's outstretched grip for the whole shot, its cold sheen lying steady across the water; only the man moves — the woodcutter bends deeper into his bow and holds it, head low, refusing with his whole back; the spirit's sleeve hangs without a stir, and the camera eases sideways past his white shoulder to keep both the shining axe and the bent man in one frame

beats.visual: the spirit stands waist-deep in the middle of the pool, risen out of the water itself with mist where his legs would be, the woodcutter stays on the bank with both feet planted on the mossed stone, dry, the pool's mist-light gone suddenly warmer: in the spirit's raised hand hangs the woodcutter's old iron axe, its short thick wooden haft worn smooth and its head a broad nicked wedge, dark seasoned steel, the very wear of the woodcutter's years on it — and the woodcutter's whole body has opened toward it; he stands at the waterline half a step into the shallows, both hands stretched out cupped and trembling, face lifted and lit with plain joy, eyes bright, the honest word already on his mouth; the spirit's deep eyes rest on him and the long white beard stirs with the smallest nod, mist folding back from between them as if the pool itself made way; the golden and silver axes are half seen resting in the crook of the spirit's other sleeve, their shine quieted, while the humble iron takes the middle of the frame like the answer to a riddle, water dripping from its haft socket in a thin bright line
beats.motion: the woodcutter's cupped hands stretch out farther and farther over the water, fingers opening, his heels lifting from the boulder as his face climbs into a broad unguarded smile, and across the pool the spirit's hand carries the old iron straight toward him at one unchanging height, the beard stirs with a small continuing nod, the mist folds back along the axe's path, and the camera tracks the iron head across the gap between god and man

beats.beat: 신령이 정직한 나무꾼에게 세 도끼를 모두 안겨 준다
beats.visual: the bank at the pool's edge, the two figures at last within arm's reach: the woodcutter stays on the bank with both feet planted on the mossed stone, dry, and the spirit, still waist-deep in the pool and touching no bank, leans from his standing water and lays the three short-hafted broad-headed axes together into the woodcutter's arms — the old iron on top, gold beneath, silver beneath that, their three sheens stacked like layered dawn — while the woodcutter receives them bowed over, staggering slightly with the unlooked-for weight, the empty haft at his feet; his face over the stacked heads is wet-eyed and laughing at once; the spirit's long brows are lifted in the mildest arch the pool has seen, beard flowing, wide sleeves spread over the giving like a roof; behind them the spiral in the water has slowed, the mist walls are thinning to threads, silver rings widen lazily toward the mossed boulders, and the first plain daylight in many shots comes back through the pines onto the two of them and the bright burden between
beats.motion: the spirit's two sleeves lower the stacked axes down into the woodcutter's waiting arms in one slow even bestowal, the man's knees flexing under the settling weight while he bows over the burden again and again in small continuous bows of thanks; the mist thinning to threads behind them, the spiral easing; daylight strengthens through the pines by one degree, and the camera holds close on the passing of the bright load

beats.beat: 욕심쟁이 이웃이 새 도끼를 연못에 던진다
beats.visual: the same bank on another bright morning, the pool mirror-still and innocent: in the woodcutter's place stands a different man — the stocky neighbor in his stiff new horsehair hat with its glossy ribbon, dark silk vest over a jeogori too clean for the slope, leather shoes planted wrong on the wet moss; he is caught at the top of a great deliberate swing, his brand-new axe flashing mirror-bright over his shoulder, pale haft gleaming, and his round face is turned not to the work but to the water, quick glittering eyes already counting, small mouth curled around a smirk; his carrier stands empty of any wood at all on the slope behind; the pool below waits black-green and unreadable, needles spiraling at the margins, the waterfall thread thin and white, and the leaning pines watch this second performance with the same stillness they gave the first
beats.motion: the neighbor hauls the shining axe around in one huge showy swing and lets it sail out spinning over the pool, blade wheeling flashes of sun as it goes, until the center water takes it and closes, rings spreading in perfect circles; he leans instantly after the throw, hat brim tipping, eyes fixed and greedy on the settling middle water; the pines and the waterfall hold still, and the camera follows the spinning axe out and down into the dark

beats.visual: the spirit stands waist-deep in the middle of the pool, risen out of the water itself with mist where his legs would be, the neighbor stays on the bank with both feet planted on the mossed stone, dry, the pool risen again: the spirit stands waist-high from the turning water within his walls of white mist, robes dry and heavy, and the spirit's long white beard reaching his chest, and his raised hand holds a Korean woodcutter's axe of solid gold, its short thick wooden haft no longer than a forearm and its head a broad heavy wedge up at beard height, no higher, exactly as before — but his face above the beard is a shade stiller than it was, the long white brows level, the deep eyes resting on the bank without any mildness arriving; on the mossed boulder the neighbor is bent far forward over the waterline, neck stretched, hands twitching open and shut at his sides, glittering eyes fixed on the gold so hard the rest of the pool has left them; his hat has slid back on its ribbon, his leather shoes grip the wet moss badly, and his shadow reaches over the water toward the shine; between them the warm gold bar lies out across the black-green surface once more, and the mist coils slow and watchful around the standing god
beats.motion: the golden axe is already raised and stays completely motionless at beard height for the whole shot, its warm bar lying steady over the water; only the man moves — the neighbor cranes farther and farther over the edge, toes flexing on the wet moss, his opening hands reaching by twitches toward the shine, hat slipping back on its ribbon; and the camera looks past the raised gold down the bar of light at the reaching man

beats.visual: the spirit stands waist-deep in the middle of the pool, risen out of the water itself with mist where his legs would be, the moment split across the water: the neighbor, both feet still on the bank's mossed boulder, has lunged out over the pool, both soft hands thrown wide open toward the golden axe, fingers spread and grasping, his round face stretched with the shout — mouth wide, eyes swallowed up by shine — his horsehair hat tipped right off his crown and hanging at his back by its glossy ribbon, one leather shoe skidding on the wet moss behind him; opposite, the spirit's long white beard reaching his chest, and the spirit's raised arm has drawn the short-hafted golden axe a hand's width back toward his chest, the wide white sleeve gathering, his face gone altogether quiet, brows beginning their descent; between the grasping hands and the withdrawing gold the pale mist-light stands like a held breath, the bar of gold on the water bending with the first disturbance of the neighbor's lunge, silver rings running out crooked from beneath his slipping foot
beats.motion: the neighbor's lunge carries him farther and farther over the water in one continuous overreach, spread fingers closing and opening on air his shoe sliding by slow inches on the moss and his hat swinging at his back; against that motion the spirit's hand holds the golden axe completely still at his chest, the crooked rings widen from the slipping foot, and the camera holds low across the bent bar of gold between them

beats.visual: an extreme close-up: the spirit's ancient face fills the entire frame from chin to bare topknot, waist-deep in the pool as always though only the face shows now — the long white eyebrows are sliding down in a slow even descent like snow deciding, shading the deep eyes until their calm goes dark as the pool's own center; the mildness has drained out of the old face without one muscle moving, the white beard hangs utterly still against the bottom frame edge, mist climbing past the wrinkled cheeks in thin steady walls; in his lowered hand, small at the frame's base, a Korean woodcutter's axe of solid gold, its short thick wooden haft no longer than a forearm and its head a broad heavy wedge rests flat on the water with its warm gleam thinning; and on that darkening water, tiny and warped beside the axe's glow, floats the reflection of the neighbor standing on the bank — hat askew, hands still reaching — bending apart on the ripples; the waterfall's white thread has gone quiet behind, and the whole pool holds its breath around the descending brows
beats.motion: the long white brows lower by slow even degrees, the shadow beneath them deepening until the eyes go dark, while below the frame's edge the golden axe sinks with the lowering hand and its warm gleam thins off the water; the mist walls climb steadily past the still face, the neighbor's small warped reflection bends and comes apart on the spreading ripples, and the camera closes with great patience on the darkened eyes

beats.visual: the pool alone in early afternoon: the spirit gone, the mist gone, the spiral gone — only flat black-green water lying mirror-still between the mossed boulders and the leaning red pines, the waterfall's thin white thread stitching quietly at the far edge as it always has; in the middle of that stillness one thing remains: a pale new wooden haft floating alone, bare of any blade, turning almost imperceptibly on the calm; pine needles drift their slow spirals at the margins around it, the pines hold their reflections without a tremble, sunlight falls plain and ordinary on moss and stone as if nothing had ever risen here; the empty bank shows only wet marks where a man's shoes slipped, already drying at the edges, and the whole frame keeps the pool's oldest expression — deep, quiet, and keeping what it keeps
beats.motion: almost nothing: the bare haft turns on the still water by slow degrees and drifts a hand's width toward the reeds of needles at the margin, one pine needle touching down beside it with rings too small to travel, the waterfall thread flickering white at the far edge, the wet shoe-marks on the bank fading as they dry; pool, pines and stone hold their long stillness, and the camera keeps one motionless frame while the ordinary light goes on

withheld: 신령이 사라진 뒤 욕심쟁이 이웃의 빈손
